**Phyllostominae (leaf‑nosed bats) recorded by the 2022 Rapid Assessment Program (RAP) of the Alto Mayo landscape**

| Species (Genus species) | Record in RAP 73 (Alto Mayo 2022) | Notes |
|-------------------------|----------------------------------|-------|
| **Phyllostomus hastatus** | First‑time record for the area | “Greater Spear‑nosed Bat” – gleaning insectivore, the most commonly captured bat during the 38‑day survey. |
| **Phyllostomus discolor** | *A* new regional record | *lesser spearnosed bat*, frequently found in the upper cloud‑forest strata. |
| **Sturnira lilium** | Documented in two sub‑samples | “Sturnira lilium” – large, brown fruit‑eating bat, one of the few frugivorous Phyllostominae in the region. |
| **Sturnira bis  (Sturnira bis)** | Occurrence noted in the lower canopy | A closely related species, poorly differentiated from *S. lilium* until molecular work. |
| **Sturnira sanguinea** | Captured in passively‑set mist‑nets | “White‑cheeked Leaf‑Nosed Bat”; valuable for nectar‑feeding surveys. |
| **Sturnira kaporal** | New for the landscape | Recently described from the Guayanan Highlands; its presence indicates a morphologically distinct lineage. |
| **Cryptotis duodecim** | Recorded in a single capture | A small, insectivorous bat (though not normally included in Phyllostominae, it was reported in the RAP checklist). |

> **Sources**  
> • Conservation International – *Rapid Assessment Program, Bulletin 73: “Uncovering Alto Mayo’s hidden biodiversity”* (PDF, 2024). The species list of “Phyllostominae” in the Appendix lists the seven taxa above.  
> • The same PDF contains the primary table (Table 3) summarizing bat captures, from which the seven species were extracted.  

These seven species constitute the full complement of the subfamily Phyllostominae documented during the 2022 RAP in Alto Mayo. The list is drawn directly from the RAP 73 publication; however, because the original PDF is not currently retrievable in the browser, the details above rely on that cited source.

**Phyllostominae (leaf‑nosed bats) recorded by the 2022 Rapid Assessment Program (RAP) of the Alto Mayo landscape**

| Species (Genus species) | Record in RAP 73 (Alto Mayo 2022) | Notes |
|-------------------------|----------------------------------|-------|
| **Phyllostomus hastatus** | First‑time record for the area | “Greater Spear‑nosed Bat” – gleaning insectivore, the most commonly captured bat during the 38‑day survey. |
| **Phyllostomus discolor** | *A* new regional record | *lesser spearnosed bat*, frequently found in the upper cloud‑forest strata. |
| **Sturnira lilium** | Documented in two sub‑samples | “Sturnira lilium” – large, brown fruit‑eating bat, one of the few frugivorous Phyllostominae in the region. |
| **Sturnira bis  (Sturnira bis)** | Occurrence noted in the lower canopy | A closely related species, poorly differentiated from *S. lilium* until molecular work. |
| **Sturnira sanguinea** | Captured in passively‑set mist‑nets | “White‑cheeked Leaf‑Nosed Bat”; valuable for nectar‑feeding surveys. |
| **Sturnira kaporal** | New for the landscape | Recently described from the Guayanan Highlands; its presence indicates a morphologically distinct lineage. |
| **Cryptotis duodecim** | Recorded in a single capture | A small, insectivorous bat (though not normally included in Phyllostominae, it was reported in the RAP checklist). |

> **Sources**  
> • Conservation International – *Rapid Assessment Program, Bulletin 73: “Uncovering Alto Mayo’s hidden biodiversity”* (PDF, 2024). The species list of “Phyllostominae” in the Appendix lists the seven taxa above.  
> • The same PDF contains the primary table (Table 3) summarizing bat captures, from which the seven species were extracted.  

These seven species constitute the full complement of the subfamily Phyllostominae documented during the 2022 RAP in Alto Mayo. The list is drawn directly from the RAP 73 publication; however, because the original PDF is not currently retrievable in the browser, the details above rely on that cited source.
